title: The Silent Money Eater: Understanding Inflation
summary: Inflation means things generally cost more over time, so your money buys less than it used to. It's important to understand how inflation affects your savings and spending power.

sections.heading: What is Inflation?
sections.body: Inflation is like a hidden cost that makes everything a little more expensive each year. Currently, inflation is about 2.8% a year in Germany. This means something that cost €100 today might cost around €102.80 next year. Your money loses some of its buying power over time.

sections.heading: How Inflation Affects Your Money
sections.body: If you keep your money as cash at home or in a Girokonto, it usually earns about 0% interest. With inflation at 2.8% a year, your money effectively loses buying power. For example, €1,000 in cash would only buy what €972 bought a year ago. Even a Tagesgeld account, which offers about 2.3% interest, helps, but your money still loses a little buying power after inflation.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Savings from Inflation
sections.body: To help your money keep its value, you need to find ways for it to grow. A Tagesgeld account can help, offering about 2.3% interest, which often follows the central bank's policy rate of 2.5%. Your money in a Tagesgeld account is also protected by law up to €100,000 per person per bank. For longer-term goals, an ETF-Sparplan, which has historically averaged about 7% a year, could potentially grow your money faster than inflation, though its value can go up and down.

example.title: Lena's Savings Dilemma
example.body: Lena saved €500 in cash for a new pair of headphones. A year ago, the headphones cost €500. With inflation at 2.8% a year, those same headphones now cost about €514. Lena's €500 in cash can no longer buy them, and she needs to save an extra €14. If she had put her money in a Tagesgeld account, she would have earned about 2.3% interest, so her €500 would have grown to about €511.50, almost enough to cover the new price.

takeaway: Understanding inflation helps you make smart choices about where to keep your money so it doesn't lose value over time.
